sources.title: Java Language Specification SE 21 §15.17.2 Division Operator /
Java SE 21 Math exact arithmetic API

claims.text: The repository source requires evaluation of a bracketed arithmetic expression but does not preserve operators, numeric domain, division/error rules, or a required evaluation algorithm.
For the declared Java integer contract, integer division truncates toward zero and an integer divisor of zero raises ArithmeticException.
The candidate uses Java Math exact arithmetic operations so representational overflow is reported instead of silently accepted under the declared fail-closed contract.

Writer and independent reviewer fixtures verify precedence, nested parentheses, unary signs, left associativity, ASCII digit grammar, the declared literal boundary, malformed-input rejection, divide-by-zero and overflow behavior for the exact candidate implementation.

boundary_tests.expected: 9223372036854775808 is rejected by exact numeric accumulation
-9223372036854775808 is rejected because the declared lexer only accepts nonnegative magnitude through Long.MAX_VALUE

findings: The repository source preserves only a request to evaluate a bracketed arithmetic expression; it does not preserve the operator set, numeric domain, division rules, malformed-input policy, or a required algorithm.
The candidate therefore labels its Java 21, ASCII integer-literal, + - * /, unary-sign, precedence, left-associativity and fail-closed error rules as answer-side contract rather than source facts.
The exact candidate Java implementation independently compiles and passes adversarial precedence, nesting, unary, associativity, malformed-input, divide-by-zero and overflow cases.

The candidate now states the subtle literal boundary precisely: a nonnegative literal magnitude may reach Long.MAX_VALUE, direct -9223372036854775808 is outside this lexer contract, while Long.MIN_VALUE may still be produced by representable arithmetic.
ASCII digit recognition in the implementation now matches the documented grammar; a full-width Unicode digit is rejected rather than misconverted.
The answer keeps alternative stack/Shunting-yard handling as a tradeoff and does not fabricate production experience.
